selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: Where did the traveler go in his thinking at the start of this passage?
questions.answer: He moved through the world of trees and plants.

questions.question: What were the trees and plants asking him to do with their world?
questions.answer: They were asking him to enter it, examine it, and understand its signs.

questions.question: What did he understand from the overall appearance of trees and plants?
questions.answer: He understood that their many kinds were all pointing together to Allah’s oneness.

questions.question: What three plant features are presented like meaningful speech?
questions.answer: The leaves, flowers, and fruits are presented that way.

questions.question: What is the first proof about?
questions.answer: It is about the clear generosity, giving, and kindness seen both in each plant and in all plants together.

questions.question: What is the main point of the second truth?
questions.answer: The main point is that the many different plant forms are carefully chosen and beautifully shaped with wisdom.

questions.question: Why does the second proof reject the idea of random chance?
questions.answer: Because the order, beauty, and special design in so many kinds show wise making, not accident.

questions.question: What qualities make this unfolding amazing in the third truth?
questions.answer: It happens with exact order, balance, beauty, and purposeful life.

questions.question: Does the passage say mistakes happen in this unfolding from seeds?
questions.answer: No. It says this happens without error or mistake.

questions.question: What feeling filled the traveler at the end of the passage?
questions.answer: He felt gratitude to Allah for having faith.

questions.question: What new realm opened before the traveler?
questions.answer: The realm of trees and plants opened before him.

questions.question: What was he told to do when he entered that realm?
questions.answer: He was told to look into it carefully and read its signs.

questions.question: Which parts of plants are mentioned as giving this message?
questions.answer: Their leaves, flowers, and fruits are mentioned.

questions.question: What does the first truth say about Allah’s giving in the plant world?
questions.answer: It says His giving and generosity are plainly seen in every plant and across all plants.

questions.question: What does this repeated kindness suggest?
questions.answer: It suggests caring and purposeful giving, not meaningless growth.

questions.question: What comes from those similar seeds?
questions.answer: Distinct plant forms come out, each in its own way.

questions.question: Why are the many plant species important in the second truth?
questions.answer: Because their endless variety still shows order and beauty, which points to wisdom.

questions.question: How many witnesses support this truth?
questions.answer: There are countless witnesses, as many as the leaves, flowers, and fruits that appear in spring.

questions.question: What lesson can a student take from the traveler’s final words?
questions.answer: A student can learn to thank Allah when seeing the signs of His power and wisdom in nature.

questions.question: What was the traveler asked to inspect after passing through mountains and plains?
questions.answer: He was asked to inspect the world of trees and plants.

questions.question: What invitation did that world give him?
questions.answer: It invited him to come in, observe, and read its signs.

questions.question: What united message came from these many kinds?
questions.answer: They all agreed in pointing to Allah’s oneness.

questions.question: What does the first truth teach about all plants together?
questions.answer: The same kindness and giving are seen across the whole plant world.

questions.question: What does the third truth begin with?
questions.answer: It begins with seeds and grains that are simple, counted, limited, and very similar.
